Marketing.heroBody: Cashly tracks your accounts, budgets, and subscriptions, so your net worth is never a guess.
Marketing.featureAccountsBody: Bring checking, savings, credit cards, and cash into one net worth number, across currencies.
Marketing.featureBudgetsBody: Set a monthly limit per category and see what's left to spend before the month runs out.
Marketing.featureSubscriptionsBody: Track recurring charges and their next billing date, so nothing renews as a surprise.
Marketing.featureInsightsBody: See income, spending, and net worth trends over time without building a spreadsheet.
Marketing.ctaBody: Free to use. Your data stays yours, exportable or deletable any time from Settings.

Terms.title: Terms of Service
Terms.s1Body: By creating an account or using Cashly, you agree to these Terms of Service. If you don't agree, please don't use the app.
Terms.s2Body: Cashly is a personal finance tracker that lets you record accounts, transactions, budgets, and subscriptions across currencies. It is a bookkeeping tool, not a bank, broker, or financial advisor, and it doesn't move money on your behalf.
Terms.s3Body: You're responsible for the accuracy of the information you enter and for keeping your login credentials secure. You must be able to form a binding contract to use Cashly, and one account is for one person — don't share credentials.
Terms.s4Body: Don't use Cashly to store data you don't have the right to store, attempt to disrupt the service, or try to access another user's data. We may suspend or terminate accounts that violate this.
Terms.s5Body: Balances, budgets, and insights shown in Cashly are calculated from the data you enter. They're provided for informational purposes only and are not financial, tax, or legal advice.
Terms.s6Body: How we collect, use, and store your data is described in the <privacyLink>Privacy Policy</privacyLink>. You can export or permanently delete your account and its data at any time from Settings.
Terms.s7Body: Cashly is provided “as is” without warranties of any kind. We don't guarantee the service will be uninterrupted or error-free, and to the fullest extent permitted by law we're not liable for any indirect or consequential damages arising from your use of it.
Terms.s8Body: We may update these terms from time to time. Continued use of Cashly after a change means you accept the updated terms.
Terms.s9Body: Questions about these terms? Reach us at <link>{email}</link>.

Privacy.title: Privacy Policy
Privacy.s1Body1: Account info: your email address, and, if you sign in with Google, your name and profile picture from your Google account.
Privacy.s1Body2: Financial data you enter: accounts, balances, transactions, budgets, and subscriptions. This data is entered by you and is not pulled from any bank or financial institution.
Privacy.s2Body: To run the app: authenticate you, show your data back to you, and calculate the balances, budgets, and insights the app displays. We don't sell your data or use it for advertising.
Privacy.s3Body: Cashly is built on Supabase, which hosts our database and handles authentication. If you sign in with Google, Google processes your sign-in under its own privacy policy. We don't share your financial data with any other third party.
Privacy.s4Body: Your data is stored in a database scoped to your account, protected by row-level security so only you can read or write it. Connections to Cashly are encrypted in transit.
Privacy.s5Body: We keep your data for as long as your account is active. You can permanently delete your account and all associated data at any time from Settings → Danger zone. Deletion is immediate and cannot be undone.
Privacy.s6Body: You can access, correct, or delete your data directly in the app at any time. If you'd like help exporting or removing your data, contact us using the details below.
Privacy.s7Body: We may update this policy from time to time. Continued use of Cashly after a change means you accept the updated policy.
Privacy.s8Body: Questions about this policy? Reach us at <link>{email}</link>.

Help.pageDescription: A field guide to every screen — from your first account to your monthly insights.
Help.gettingStartedIntro: Cashly onboards you in four short steps before dropping you at your dashboard. Every step saves as you go, so if you refresh mid-setup you resume instead of starting over.
Help.step1Body: Pre-filled from your email — used to greet you around the app.
Help.step2Body: The currency your net worth, budgets, and insights are measured in.
Help.step3Body: Name it, choose a type — checking, savings, cash, or investment — and set a starting balance.
Help.step4Body: Add a credit card from its name, currency and last 4, and import its first statement right there. Skippable.
Help.bankCalloutBody: Credit cards, loans, and bank selection all live on the full Accounts page instead — onboarding just needs one account to get you in the door. Add a bank once you have a second account, so transfers between them can qualify for the same-bank fee waiver.
Help.overviewIntro: Overview is home base — the first screen you land on after signing in. It's built to answer "where do I stand right now?" in one glance.
Help.overviewNetWorth: Net worth — the headline figure, rolled up across every account.
Help.overviewStats: This month's stats — income, spending, and budget used so far.
Help.overviewUpcoming: Upcoming — a rail of what's due next: subscription charges and loan payments.
Help.overviewZeroState: No accounts yet? Overview shows starter cards linking straight to Accounts, Budgets, and Subscriptions instead of an empty page.
Help.overviewFxWarning: If exchange rates can't be fetched, Overview and Insights say so — foreign holdings are counted 1:1 until rates return, and the warning tells you which currencies are affected.
Help.navNote: On mobile, Settings lives in the header, not the bottom nav. A floating Quick Add button for new transactions follows you everywhere.
Help.accountsIntro: Everything you own or owe lives here, grouped into four sections: Accounts (checking, savings, cash, investment), Credit cards, Loans, and Property & assets.
Help.quickAddCardNote: Need just a card, fast? Use "Quick add card" next to the Credit cards heading — it only asks for the name, currency, and last 4 digits, and you can fill in the limit and dates later from your first statement.
Help.cardGroupNote: A card group bundles multiple currency lines of one physical card (say, a USD and a CAD line) into a single tile.
Help.sameBankCalloutBody: Set the same bank on two accounts, and a Payment between them skips the network fee automatically — no toggling required.
Help.accountPageBalance: Balance (or amount owed) as the hero figure, plus a balance-over-time chart
Help.accountPageUtilization: Utilization and next due date, for credit cards
Help.accountPageCashback: Cashback earned so far this year, for credit cards, read off your imported statements
Help.accountPageCostOfOwnership: What the card charges you to hold it — fees and insurance billed this year, read off your imported statements
Help.accountPageSpend: A spend-by-category ring for the current calendar month, for credit cards, counting only what was charged to that card and in that card's own currency
Help.accountPageAmortization: A full amortization schedule, for loans
Help.accountPageActivity: A transfer-fee summary and the complete activity feed
Help.accountPageActions: Edit, Archive / Restore, or Delete (with a confirmation step)
Help.cardFaceBody: Credit cards are drawn as the physical object. Cashly reads the card's name to pick its colour and its network mark — an Amex Platinum comes out silver, a Visa Infinite black — and the face appears on the card's own page as well as in the list.
Help.cardFaceReroll: Not the colour you expected? Clear the colour field and save. Cashly guesses again from the name, and a colour you type in yourself is always kept as-is.
Help.accountPageFace: The card face, sitting beside the balance, so you know at a glance which card you're on.
Help.accountPageLines: For a card in a group, its other currency lines sit in a strip right under the face — one click to switch between them, and the group's name sits at the top of the page.
Help.subBrand: Logos and colours appear on their own — Cashly recognises the service from the name you gave it. Anything it doesn't recognise keeps its initial, which is a finished look, not a missing one. Renaming a subscription makes it look again.
Help.statementsBody: You can import a statement from several places: Overview asks for one when a statement is due, the Import statement button sits in the Wallet header and on the Insights cards that need one, each card's own page keeps it next to its history, and setup offers it at the end. If you have no card yet, you create one right there from three fields — name, currency and last 4 — because the limit, closing day and due day fill themselves in from the first statement. Upload the PDF — password-protected files are supported, with a retry if you mistype the password. Cashly splits it into sections (one per currency line on the card), you confirm which account each maps to, then Confirm to import. If a section is in a currency none of your card's lines uses, you can add that line right there instead of leaving to create it. Installments arrive as their own section carrying their own limit and balance, so they get their own line — named "· Installments" rather than "· DOP", so it doesn't read as a second card. This creates the underlying transactions and powers the cost-of-carry and cashback figures in Insights. Cashback is read off each statement and counted once per closing date, so re-importing the same PDF corrects the figure instead of doubling it. Statements up to 10 MB are accepted.
Help.triageBody: When an import finishes, the app categorises what it recognises and asks you about the rest — one merchant at a time, not one transaction at a time. Every answer is saved as a rule, so the next statement asks less. If you leave some of it, any statement takes you back to that screen from the card's page.
Help.triageMockMerchantOne: SM NACIONAL METRO PLZA SANTO DOMINGO-DO
Help.transactionsIntro: Three kinds of entry cover everything: Expense, Income, and Payment.
Help.typePayment: Payment — a transfer between your own accounts, or paying down a credit card or loan. Cross-currency payments show a live "lands as X" preview of the converted amount.
Help.toggleTax: Transfer tax — charged when money leaves your checking or savings account. Moving money between your own cash and bank accounts is free of it; so is spending cash or swiping a card, since no account is debited. Paying a credit card or a loan is taxed, because that money goes to the bank even though the card is in your name.
Help.toggleFee: Network fee — off unless you add it, because only some transfers carry one. Always waived within the same bank.
Help.addingBody: Quick Add opens on the amount with a numeric keypad: type it, tap a category, save. Categories are ordered by the ones you use most, and the account is the source of your last expense or payment. More details opens every remaining field — destination, rate, date, notes, budget exclusion and the tax and fee switches — in the same panel. To start from the full form instead, use Add transaction on an account's page. Every entry takes a free-text Note, the one field that stays editable on statement-imported rows, where the description belongs to your bank.
Help.findingBody: Search matches a transaction's description, its notes, and — when you type a figure like 1,500 — its amount. Filters run against your whole history, not just what's on screen, and the ledger loads more as you scroll until it tells you you've reached the end.
Help.merchantCalloutBody: Transactions created from a statement import keep their original amount and date locked — you just confirm the category, and can save "always categorize this merchant" so it's automatic next time.
Help.budgetsIntro: Budgets run month by month, one row per category. Navigate between months, and set an amount for each category inline.
Help.budgetsCategory: Create categories with a name, emoji, and color
Help.budgetsInline: Type a monthly amount directly into a category's row
Help.budgetsProgress: Each row's progress bar changes color as you approach or pass the limit
Help.budgetsHeader: The header totals budget, amount used, and what's left, across all categories
Help.copyCalloutBody: Duplicates last month's amounts forward, so you're not re-typing the same numbers every month.
Help.subscriptionsIntro: Track recurring charges — streaming, software, memberships — separately from one-off spending.
Help.subName: Set a name, brand, amount and currency
Help.subCycle: Choose a billing cycle — weekly, monthly, yearly, or custom — anchored to a specific day
Help.subLink: Link an account and category, and toggle active/inactive
Help.subViews: Switch between grid and table views
Help.subLogCharge: The page totals your monthly-equivalent spend and shows each subscription's next charge date. When a charge actually bills, hit Add charge to record the transaction.
Help.insightsIntro: A month-navigable analytics view that turns your accounts and transactions into a handful of answers.
Help.insightsSpend: Spend distribution — where your money went, by category
Help.insightsDebt: Debt health — credit utilization and a loan summary
Help.insightsCashflow: Cash-flow trend and spending pace across the month
Help.insightsBudget: Expenses vs. budget, category by category
Help.insightsCarry: Cost of carry — an estimated finance charge on card balances, at each card's APR, sourced from imported statements
Help.insightsCashback: Cashback — what each card has earned you this year, in that card's own currency
Help.insightsCostOfOwnership: Cost of ownership — annual fees, insurance and membership charges each card billed this year, never subtracted from its benefits
Help.insightsLoanInterest: Loan interest — how much of each loan payment went to interest rather than to principal
Help.askIntro: A text box that answers questions about your own numbers in plain words — English or Spanish, whichever you're using. Cashly reads your data to answer, and writes a short reply with the real figures in it.
Help.askAnswers: Good questions: spending by category over any date range, what went on one specific card between two dates, what a balance is now, what's due and when, how a month tracked against its budget.
Help.askReadOnly: It can only read. There is no question you can ask that changes a transaction, a budget, or an account — and it only ever sees your own data, never anyone else's.
Help.askLimits: It answers from what's recorded. If you haven't imported a statement or logged a transaction, it can't know about it — and it will say so rather than guess.
Help.askMockQuestion: How much did I spend on transportation last month?
Help.askMockAnswer: RD$8,420 across 14 transactions — about 12% more than June.
Help.settingsTheme: Theme — light or dark, from here or the sidebar
Help.settingsAccount: Sign out, or delete your account (with confirmation)
Help.rulesBody: Settings → Category rules holds everything the app has learned: the text it looks for in a transaction, and the category it assigns. The number says how many lines of your statements match that rule — one matching 40 lines is working, one matching 0 probably has a typo. You can shorten the text so it covers every branch of a merchant. Editing a rule changes future imports; it does not recategorise what you already saved.
Help.footerNote: This guide mirrors the app's own navigation, top to bottom.
